from_quote: In the recognition which the Landholder professes to make "of what occurred to my advantage,"
rationale: Number II of Martin's address continues his answer to the Landholder, quoting the part of the Landholder's address to Martin that recognizes "whatever occurred to your advantage"; the essay is worked out from that subject and from Number I, which names the Maryland Journal of February 29.

from_quote: this Constitution and the laws of the United States, which shall be made in pursuance thereof, and all treaties made, or which shall be made, under the authority of the United States, shall be the supreme law of the land, and the judges in every state shall be bound thereby, any thing in the Constitution or the laws of any state to the contrary notwithstanding.
rationale: The paragraph quotes in full, in quotation marks, the clause of Article VI that it calls "the clause which enacts" that the Constitution, laws and treaties are the supreme law of the land.
to_quote: This Constitution, and the Laws of the United States which shall be made in Pursuance thereof; and all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States, shall be the supreme Law of the Land; and the Judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any Thing in the Constitution or Laws of any State to the Contrary notwithstanding.

from_quote: voted an appeal should lay to the supreme judiciary of the United States, for the correction of all errors both in law and fact
rationale: The paragraph quotes in quotation marks the Landholder's statement in his address to Martin about Martin's vote on appeals, and then "the Landholder also says" about the nine-state clause.
to_quote: an appeal should lay to the Supreme Judiciary of the United States, for the correction of all errors, both in law and fact

from_quote: as the clause now stands, an appeal being given in general terms from the inferior courts, both as to law and fact
rationale: The paragraph refers to "the clause" as it "now stands" giving an appeal "both as to law and fact", echoing the words of the appellate-jurisdiction clause of Article III, Section 2.
to_quote: appellate Jurisdiction, both as to Law and Fact

from_quote: the clause that declares nine states to be sufficient to put the government in motion
rationale: The paragraph names "the clause that declares nine states to be sufficient", which only the ratification clause of Article VII fits.

from_quote: the power of suspending the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus
rationale: The paragraph names the general government's power of "suspending the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus" and "the power given to it", echoing the words of Article I, Section 9, Clause 2.

rationale: The paragraph identifies by number "that part of the sixth article which requires an oath to be taken by the persons there mentioned, in support of the constitution".
